features.name: any_assertive_phrase_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain the assertive phrase "in fact" or "as a matter of fact"?
features.spec: import json,re; parse df['OC_comments'] with json.loads to a list of strings; if missing/malformed/not a list return null; empty list -> 0. Return 1 if any comment matches re.search(r"\b(in fact|as a matter of fact)\b", comment, re.I), else 0. Mechanical literal match: no semantic filtering, quoted text and any outcome announcements inside comments are not excluded.

h0: any_assertive_phrase_comment has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Rows with any_assertive_phrase_comment = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than rows with 0.
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change); association only, not causal. Assertive phrases operationalized as only the two literal phrases given ("in fact", "as a matter of fact"), case-insensitive; other assertive wording not counted. Row-level any-presence chosen; comments are unordered and no per-comment outcomes exist, so the specific comment using the phrase cannot be linked to the delta. Raw text may include quoted text from others, or post-outcome announcements; not filtered. "In fact" also has non-assertive uses; accepted as part of the literal definition.
